 They want the previous "longer version" (the one in blockquote) reproduced as plain text, easy copy-paste. So just
 output the longer version without ">" formatting. No commentary.

 Which "longer version"? My second message's long version (the blockquote one). Deliver that as plain text lines.

 They don't actually look the same — the difference is that "thinking" is an animation and "waiting" is chrome.

 Working: the TUI is ticking a braille spinner (U+2801–28FF) in the viewport, and the current frame stays on screen
 between ticks, so a single tmux capture-pane -p sees it. No word matching — "working"/"thinking" fired on token
 counters and file paths, so the rule is the whole glyph block.

 Blocked: the pane draws the question itself. For pi that's the ask-user-question hint line, matched on its
 invariant prefix ("Enter to select · ↑/↓ to navigate") with all whitespace squeezed out, so a mid-word wrap in a
 narrow pane still matches. For grok it's the card that holds the turn open — 1/4:select, Tab:next answer, ◇ Waiting
 on answers for ….

 Blocked is tested before working on purpose, so a question can't be masked by an incidental spinner. And the screen
 isn't the only witness: if the pane's foreground process is gone or back at a shell, the state is idle no matter
 what leftover TUI frame is painted.

 The other half of that confusion is idle-vs-finished — a pane that already worked and stopped is pinned via the
 tmux pane option @tmuxrd_finished, so it renders as finished rather than idle.

 Honest limit: it's a scraper. A TUI that streams plain prose with neither a spinner nor a question card reads as
 unknown, not working.
